meta.format: chunk = {seed, index, x, z, cols, columnDefs}; cols[i] is an index into columnDefs in x-major / z-minor ChunkUtil.indexColumn order; a column def is [tint, biomeId, zoneId, envRuns, blockRuns, parentBiomeId, borderDistance, biomeIndex, cellX, cellY]; envRuns entries are [minYInclusive, maxYInclusive, environmentId]; blockRuns entries are [yStartInclusive, yEndInclusive, blockId, rotationIndex, filler, fluidId, fluidLevel, priorityByte] — a run ends when ANY of the eight values changes; the ids resolve through the palettes; parentBiomeId is the raw tile biome BEFORE the custom-biome overlay, borderDistance is the zone border distance, biomeIndex is the raw BiomePatternGenerator.getBiomeIndex value and cellX/cellY are the nearest biome-grid cell — the last four are debug references, not part of the parity target
meta.boot: the vanilla CoreServer asset pipeline booted by RegistryDumper (AssetRegistryLoader over Assets/Assets.zip mounted as a zip FileSystem) + an AssetModule singleton stub whose base pack is the UNPACKED asset tree (Assets/extracted), so the world-gen AssetFileSystem resolves world files and prefabs through the disk tree — the same tree the Rust port walks (testdata/Default is byte-identical to Assets/extracted/Server/World/Default)
meta.world: Server/World/Default inside the unpacked asset tree (byte-identical to the extracted testdata/Default copy; the AssetFileSystem relativizes every path against the stub pack root)
meta.load: the FULL ChunkGeneratorJsonLoader.load() PER SEED with SeedString(Integer.toString(seed)) + SeedStringResource(PrefabStoreRoot.DEFAULT, config) — the golden seed-label convention of Phase2Dumper/LoaderDumper (the vanilla provider would use the constant "ChunkGenerator" label); the load includes the prefab store (World.json PrefabStore) and EventHandler.acquire(worldPath)
meta.generate: new ChunkGeneratorExecution(seed, generator, generatedChunk).execute(seed) on the dumper's main thread — the same work ChunkGenerator.generate(...) submits to its worker pool; every random stream is seeded from (seed, coordinates), so the thread does not matter
meta.stages: tint mapping → environment mapping → BlockPopulator → CavePopulator → PrefabPopulator → WaterPopulator (the execute() stage order)
meta.notDumped: the BlockPhysics support values and the per-block Holder<ChunkStore> states (the Rust port documents BlockPhysics as a no-op), the entity chunk and the block components (deferred per REMAINING.md §2); the tint and the environment columns ARE dumped
meta.biomeLookup: per column through the generator's own cached getZoneBiomeResultAt(seed, worldX, worldZ) AFTER the execution — it consumes no generation stream (the caches are keyed by seed + coordinates)
meta.deterministic: no timestamps are written; the dump is byte-identical across runs
